name: Lucius
overview: Lucius is a male figure mentioned in the New Testament as a kinsman of the Apostle Paul, highlighting a familial connection within the early Christian community. His tribal affiliation and additional personal details are not recorded in Scripture. This brief mention situates Lucius within the network of early believers closely associated with Paul.
namesAndTitles: The name Lucius appears once in Scripture without an explicit meaning provided. It is presented simply as a proper name without additional titles or divine naming significance.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record family relationships for Lucius beyond his identification as a kinsman of Paul. No further relational details are provided in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Lucius holds significance as a relative of Paul, indicating the personal connections that supported Paul’s ministry and the spread of the gospel. His mention in Romans 16:21 places him among those who were part of the early Christian fellowship, underscoring the relational ties that encouraged and strengthened the apostolic mission.
